value.title: Introduction to Transformer Context and Embedding
value.summary: This chapter explains how transformer models process context size and the role of embedding layers in converting input tokens into numerical vectors. It introduces the concept of the un-embedding matrix (WU) and its function in mapping final layer vectors back to vocabulary probabilities, highlighting its contribution to the model's parameter count.

value.title: Softmax Function and Probability Distributions
value.summary: The chapter provides a detailed explanation of the softmax function, describing how it transforms arbitrary numerical outputs into valid probability distributions by exponentiating inputs and normalizing them to sum to one. It emphasizes the function's role in ensuring outputs are between 0 and 1 and add up to 1, which is essential for next-word prediction in language models.

value.title: Temperature Scaling and Sampling Behavior
value.summary: This section explores the effect of temperature (T) on softmax outputs, showing how higher temperatures produce flatter, more uniform distributions favoring diversity, while lower temperatures sharpen the distribution toward the most probable output. It demonstrates this with examples of story generation using different temperature settings and discusses the practical API limit of T ≤ 2.

value.title: Attention Mechanism Foundations
value.summary: The chapter lays the groundwork for understanding attention by reviewing key components: word embeddings, dot products for measuring similarity, and the use of matrix multiplication with learnable parameters. These concepts are presented as essential prerequisites for grasping the attention mechanism.

value.title: Advanced Topics and Patron Support
value.summary: The final chapter previews the next chapter on attention mechanisms, available to Patreon supporters, and expresses gratitude to patrons. It also notes that the full version will be released publicly in one to two weeks, depending on feedback.
